old: Here we introduce Partial Effective Information Decomposition (PEID), an intervention-based framework that resolves joint effective information into non-negative synergistic contributions associated with specific variable groups. Motivated by the axiomatic framework of PID \cite{Bertschinger2013SharedInformation}, PEID quantifies synergy directly from effective information under a common factorized maximum-entropy intervention, without specifying a redundancy function. These contributions are exactly additive across nested partitions, enabling the construction of the Synergy Partition Tree (SPT) which captures their hierarchical organization across variable groups and interaction orders without enumerating the full partial-information lattice.
new: Here we introduce Partial Effective Information Decomposition (PEID), an intervention-based framework that resolves joint effective information into non-negative synergistic contributions associated with specific variable groups. \rev{PEID quantifies synergy directly from effective information under a common factorized maximum-entropy intervention. Its two-source expression coincides with PID synergy for redundancy measures satisfying non-negativity, Identity and probabilistic left monotonicity \cite{Harder2013BivariateRedundancy,Rauh2017ExtractableSharedInformation}.} These contributions are exactly additive across nested partitions, enabling the construction of the Synergy Partition Tree (SPT) which captures their hierarchical organization across variable groups and interaction orders without enumerating the full partial-information lattice.

location: Discussion: link between independence and PID
old: Across biological, Earth and social systems, \rev{the models examined here suggest that }collective behaviour emerges not simply from pairwise couplings, but from how causal interactions are hierarchically organized and reconfigured across variable groups, states and scales. PEID makes this organization visible by treating synergy as irreducible joint causal information under a specified intervention: independent maximum-entropy interventions strip away the redundancy induced by observed source dependence, so that the excess of joint effective information over individual contributions isolates genuinely synergistic causal atoms. The SPT then arranges these atoms into nested partitions across interaction orders without enumerating the combinatorial PID lattice, revealing not merely how much synergy exists but how it is hierarchically organized and reconfigured across states and scales.
new: Across biological, Earth and social systems, \rev{the models examined here suggest that }collective behaviour emerges not simply from pairwise couplings, but from how causal interactions are hierarchically organized and reconfigured across variable groups, states and scales. \rev{PEID quantifies the joint causal information generated under factorized maximum-entropy interventions. For two sources, the excess of joint effective information over the single-source contributions equals conditional mutual information and, under the stated redundancy properties, PID synergy. For larger source sets, SPT resolves the integrated information into additive contributions across nested partitions, revealing how joint causal information is organized and reconfigured across states and scales.}
